arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon) successfully compromised a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) via malicious Outlook macro execution. The initial payload, 'chrome_helper.exe', was delivered as a weaponized attachment and executed PowerShell to deploy a ShadowPad variant via process hollowing and DLL sideloading through rundll32.exe. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23) and a dynamic DNS domain (update.ns3.ezdns.cc), exhibiting beaconing behavior. Post-compromise activities included host file modification, SMB-based lateral movement attempts, and privilege escalation reconnaissance. The incident was detected through IDS alerts (Cobalt Strike beacon pattern) and EDR telemetry (anomalous process chain). Response actions were attempted but failed due to misalignment with actual compromised asset.
